analyzed_vuln.description: `dissect_softether_tuples` does not check whether parsing the first tuple value succeeded. When `dissect_softether_type(first_tuple_type, ...)` returns 0, the helper leaves the payload pointer unchanged, parses the second value from the same bytes, and can return a nonzero overall tuple size if that second interpretation succeeds. The failed first parse has already populated `first_value->type`, pointer, and attacker-controlled `value_size`, so `dissect_softether_host_fqdn` treats it as valid and passes that size to `strncpy`, causing an out-of-bounds read/use-after-poison. In this PoV, the same truncated length-prefixed value fails as `VALUE_STR` but succeeds as `VALUE_DATA`, since DATA consumes one fewer content byte.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A packet must reach SoftEther detection with a payload of at least 99 bytes and pass the host/FQDN parser prefix checks. The PoV also uses a large tuple count whose `tuple_count * 8` check wraps, and preceding tuples arrange for the FQDN/hostname state flag to be set. The crashing tuple declares first type `VALUE_STR` and second type `VALUE_DATA`; after its 8-byte type header, only 13 bytes remain: a 4-byte declared length of 10 followed by 9 data bytes. Parsing as STR fails because 14 bytes are required, but leaves `val1` containing type STR, size 10, and a pointer to those 9 bytes. Because the failure is ignored, the same encoding is reparsed as DATA and succeeds with a 13-byte consumption. The caller therefore executes `strncpy(..., val1.value_str, 10)`, reading one byte beyond the packet allocation.

args: Analyze the SoftEther parser vulnerability in `dissect_softether_tuples` and related parsing in `src/lib/protocols/softether.c`. Identify all arithmetic overflow and failed-parse state issues relevant to malformed tuple counts/values, and recommend the smallest root-cause fix that preserves valid parsing.

The sanitizer report shows `dissect_softether_host_fqdn` calling `strncpy` with an attacker-controlled length from a failed first tuple parse. `dissect_softether_tuples` apparently ignores a zero return from `dissect_softether_type` for the first value, leaves the payload unchanged, then parses the second type from the same bytes. The PoV uses first type VALUE_STR and second VALUE_DATA, with 13 remaining bytes encoding declared length 10 plus 9 content bytes; STR needs 14 and fails, DATA consumes 13 and succeeds. The report also says a large tuple count passes a `tuple_count * 8` check through integer wrap. We need inspect the complete parser and fix root causes, likely requiring immediate failure after either value parser fails plus division/subtraction-based bounds checks.
